name: brain-control
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School teaching illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif title and labels, pale blue rounded label panels, soft shaded friendly anatomical art. Pink brain, golden nerves; teal sensory-message arrows and orange motor-command arrows. No gore, watermark, tiny text, or blood-vessel diagrams. SQUARE 1:1 composition. Exact title "The brain is the control center". Large anatomically recognizable SIDE VIEW of a pink human brain in center, with three spacious small vignettes around it. Upper-left vignette: eye and ear, caption "Receive information". Right vignette: hand and forearm reaching for a ball, caption "Direct movement". Bottom-left vignette: a child reading a book, caption "Remember and learn". Connect each job vignette to brain with neutral thin navy lines, no directional neural pathways needed. Brain is uniformly natural pink with subtle shaded folds, no colored brain regions and no named lobes. The examples illustrate shared functions, not precise localization. Balanced clear uncluttered composition with readable captions.

name: message-directions
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School teaching illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif title and labels, pale blue rounded label panels, soft shaded friendly anatomical art. Pink brain, golden nerves; teal sensory-message arrows and orange motor-command arrows. No gore, watermark, tiny text, or blood-vessel diagrams. PORTRAIT 4:5 composition. Exact title "Messages travel in two directions". Simplified front-view neutral school-age body outline, brain visible in head, spinal cord running vertically down center of torso, fine golden peripheral nerves branching to arms and legs. A clearly TEAL route begins at viewer-left fingertips and runs UP arm toward spinal cord, then UP to brain: every teal arrowhead points INWARD and UPWARD toward central nervous system. A separate ORANGE route begins at brain, runs DOWN spinal cord, then DOWN viewer-right leg to a thigh muscle: every orange arrowhead points OUTWARD/DOWNWARD toward muscle. Keep the two routes separated and legible. Accurate leader labels "Brain", "Spinal cord", "Nerves". Bottom legend teal arrow "Sensory: toward brain or spinal cord"; orange arrow "Motor: toward muscles". No arrows from leg to brain in orange, and no teal arrow outward to hand. No organs besides nervous-system illustration and target muscle. Fully within frame, large legible type.

name: spinal-reflex
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School teaching illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif title and labels, pale blue rounded label panels, soft shaded friendly anatomical art. Pink brain, golden nerves; teal sensory-message arrows and orange motor-command arrows. No gore, watermark, tiny text, or blood-vessel diagrams. SQUARE 1:1 composition. Exact title "Reflexes help you respond quickly". A simple explanatory SCHEMATIC, not dense medical cross-section. At LEFT: hand and bent arm pulling away from a hot ceramic cup, with subtle heat squiggles, no burns or injury. At RIGHT CENTER: enlarged vertical spinal cord segment, label "Spinal cord". A TEAL sensory path goes from fingertip skin toward spinal cord, with clear arrowheads pointing RIGHT to spinal cord, label "Sensory message". An ORANGE motor path leaves spinal cord and travels LEFT to an upper-arm muscle, clear leftward arrowheads, label "Motor command". Make these two paths a clear fast spinal loop. At UPPER RIGHT: small brain, connected to spinal cord by a SEPARATE THINNER teal upward arrow, caption "Brain receives information too". No orange path from brain to spinal loop. Bottom short caption "The spinal cord starts this fast response." Large labels and roomy layout. Hand movement arrow away from cup is neutral navy, visually distinct from nerve-message arrows.

name: chosen-action
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School teaching illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif title and labels, pale blue rounded label panels, soft shaded friendly anatomical art. Pink brain, golden nerves; teal sensory-message arrows and orange motor-command arrows. No gore, watermark, tiny text, or blood-vessel diagrams. WIDE 2:1 landscape composition. Exact title "Actions you choose". Three large sequential vignettes from LEFT to RIGHT, separated with ample white space. LEFT: child side-profile eye looking toward an approaching colorful ball, caption "Eye notices ball". CENTER: large pink brain, caption "Brain chooses response". RIGHT: forearm and open hand catching that same ball, a simple red upper-arm muscle highlighted under faint skin, caption "Arm muscles move". One large TEAL arrow goes LEFT-TO-RIGHT from the eye vignette TO the brain, label "Sensory message". One large ORANGE arrow goes LEFT-TO-RIGHT from brain TO the arm vignette, label "Motor command". Arrowheads point toward their destinations, not backward. No spinal reflex loop, no neurons or detailed brain regions. Keep all captions large and inside canvas. This is a simplified chosen action sequence, not a time-series of three different children.
